The inline `session?.email?.split('@').at(1) ?? ''` domain extraction duplicates the same logic used in `BaseOnboardingPersonalDetails.tsx` and reimplements the existing `getEmailDomain(email)` helper in `src/libs/LoginUtils.ts`.

Use the shared helper instead:

```tsx
import {getEmailDomain} from '@libs/LoginUtils';
// ...
companyDomain: session?.email ? getEmailDomain(session.email) : '',
```

The company-domain extraction `workEmail.split('@').at(1) ?? ''` is duplicated here and in `BaseOnboardingWorkspaces.tsx` (`session?.email?.split('@').at(1) ?? ''`), and it reimplements logic that already exists as a shared helper. `getEmailDomain(email)` in `src/libs/LoginUtils.ts` already extracts an email's domain.

Reuse the existing helper instead of the inline `.split('@')`:

```tsx
import {getEmailDomain} from '@libs/LoginUtils';
// ...
companyDomain: getEmailDomain(workEmail),
```

This inline `returnToOriginReport` closure repeats the exact `dismissOnboardingModalBeforeExit()` + `Navigation.navigate(ROUTES.REPORT_WITH_ID.getRoute(originReportID ?? conciergeReportID))` logic already defined in `BaseOnboardingPrivateDomain.tsx` and `BaseOnboardingWorkspaces.tsx`. Besides duplicating across files, it is also re-created inside this effect on every run.

Extract the behavior into a shared reusable hook (e.g. `useReturnToOriginReport`) and call it from all three onboarding screens rather than redefining the closure.

This `returnToOriginReport` function is a verbatim copy of the same closure in `BaseOnboardingPrivateDomain.tsx` and `BaseOnboardingWorkEmail.tsx` (`dismissOnboardingModalBeforeExit()` + `Navigation.navigate(ROUTES.REPORT_WITH_ID.getRoute(originReportID ?? conciergeReportID))`). Three independent copies of the same navigation logic increases maintenance overhead and risks the copies diverging.

Consolidate into a single shared hook (e.g. `useReturnToOriginReport`) that owns `originReportID`/`conciergeReportID` and the navigation, and use it in all three onboarding screens instead of re-declaring the function per file.

This header-label expression `${toLocaleOrdinalWithWords(1)} ${translate('common.approver').toLowerCase()}` (falling back to `translate('common.approver')`) is identical to the one in `src/pages/workspace/members/WorkspaceMemberDetailsPage.tsx`. The same "First approver" / "Approver" copy is generated in two places, so a future copy change has to be made twice and can silently diverge.

Move the label logic into a single shared helper and call it from both the table header and the member profile row:

```ts
label: getApproverLabel(hasMultiLevelWorkflow, translate, toLocaleOrdinalWithWords),
```

`NON_EXPENSE_CREATION_IOU_TYPES` and `getCreatedTransactionID` duplicate the identical `nonExpenseCreationIOUTypes` set and expense-creation-action logic that this same PR adds to `src/libs/ReportActionsUtils.ts` (`getExpenseCreationIOUActionForTransactionID`, exported from that module). The comment, the Set of IOU action types, and the filtering rule are the same in both places, so a future change to which IOU types count as "expense creation" must be made twice.

Reuse the shared helper instead of re-declaring the set and logic here. Import `getExpenseCreationIOUActionForTransactionID` (or extract the shared `getCreatedTransactionID`/set into `ReportActionsUtils` and import it) so `collectParentReportActions` calls the single source of truth.

`useCurrencyListActions()` is now called twice in the same component — once here for `convertToDisplayString` and again on the next line for `getCurrencyDecimals`. This duplicates the hook invocation unnecessarily. Every other file in this PR added `convertToDisplayString` by extending the existing destructuring on a single call.

Destructure both values from one call instead:

```tsx
const {getCurrencyDecimals, convertToDisplayString} = useCurrencyListActions();
```

and remove the duplicate call on the following line.

`isEligibleForTaskStatus` is a near line-for-line duplicate of the existing `isEligibleForStatus`: both read the `STATUS` filter, return `true` when empty, branch on `status.isNegated` iterating `Object.keys(<mapping>).some(...)` with an `isExcluded` check, then fall through to `status.value.some(...)`. The accompanying `taskStatusActionMapping`/`isValidTaskStatus` also mirror `expenseStatusActionMapping`/`isValidExpenseStatus`. The only real differences are the mapping object and the validator.

Consider extracting the shared control flow into one helper parameterized by the mapping and validator, e.g.:

```ts
function isEligibleForStatusFilter<T>(
    currentQueryJSON: SearchQueryJSON | undefined,
    report: T,
    mapping: Record<string, (report: T, ...rest: never[]) => boolean>,
    isValidStatus: (status: unknown) => boolean,
    ...predicateArgs: unknown[]
) { /* shared branch/negation/some logic */ }
```

so `isEligibleForStatus` and `isEligibleForTaskStatus` both delegate to it instead of copying the branching.

The skeleton row geometry here duplicates `ForYouSkeleton.tsx`: the same `ICON_SIZE`/`ICON_BORDER_RADIUS` constants (with the identical `getWidgetItemIconContainerStyle` comment), the same `BAR_HEIGHT = 12`, and the same row math (`iconTextGap = styles.gap3.gap`, `rowHeight = ICON_SIZE + styles.pv3.paddingVertical * 2`, `horizontalPadding = shouldUseNarrowLayout ? styles.ph5.paddingHorizontal : styles.ph8.paddingHorizontal`) plus the icon `SkeletonRect`. If the real row layout changes, both files must be kept in sync.

Extract the shared row geometry (constants + `iconTextGap`/`rowHeight`/`horizontalPadding` derivation, and the icon rect renderer) into a shared helper/hook (e.g. `useSkeletonRowGeometry`) and consume it from both `HomePageSkeleton.tsx` and `ForYouSkeleton.tsx`.

The latest-error extraction (`Object.values(...).at(-1)` + `typeof latestError === 'string' ? latestError : undefined`) is duplicated across four bank-connection screens. Consolidate it into a single shared helper (e.g. `getLatestErrorMessage(errors)`) and call it here instead of repeating the two lines.

```ts
const errorMessage = getLatestErrorMessage(addNewCard?.errors);
```

Same `showConfirmModal({...unlockAlreadyRequested...})` block duplicated across `SettlementButton/index.tsx`, `UnlockBankAccount.tsx`, and `WalletPage/index.tsx`. Consolidate into one reusable helper and call it here.

```tsx
showUnlockAlreadyRequestedModal(showConfirmModal, translate);
```

Same `showConfirmModal({...unlockAlreadyRequested...})` block duplicated across `SettlementButton/index.tsx`, `UnlockBankAccount.tsx`, and `WorkflowsPaymentsTab.tsx`. Consolidate into one reusable helper and call it here.

```tsx
showUnlockAlreadyRequestedModal(showConfirmModal, translate);
```

This is the same `showConfirmModal({...unlockAlreadyRequested...})` block that also appears in `SettlementButton/index.tsx`, `WalletPage/index.tsx`, and `WorkflowsPaymentsTab.tsx`. The duplication should be consolidated.

Replace all four occurrences with a single shared helper, e.g.:

```tsx
showUnlockAlreadyRequestedModal(showConfirmModal, translate);
```

`useTravelBillingFeedsForFeedSelector` is a line-for-line duplicate of the existing `src/hooks/useExpensifyCardFeedsForFeedSelector.ts` — same Onyx subscriptions (`PRIVATE_EXPENSIFY_CARD_SETTINGS`, `POLICY`, `DOMAIN`), same `currentUserAccountID` derivation, same early return, same `getAdmin*FeedEntries` + `partition*FeedsForSelector` flow, differing only in the two util function names it calls. Maintaining two copies of the same subscription/partition wiring adds maintenance overhead and bug risk.

Once the underlying utils are consolidated (see the util-file comment), fold this into a single shared hook that takes the program-specific predicate (or reuse one hook with a parameter) instead of copying the whole hook.

This is the fourth copy of the `Str.removeSMSDomain(name ? name : (email ?? ''))` fallback that used to live inside the deleted `getUserNameByEmail` helper (see also `AssigneeStep.tsx` lines 103/107 and `CardNameStep.tsx` line 57).

Extract the logic into a single reusable helper and call it here (e.g. `getUserNameFromDetail(assigneeDisplayName, data?.assigneeEmail ?? '')`) instead of inlining the ternary + `removeSMSDomain` in each file.

This repeats the exact `Str.removeSMSDomain(name ? name : (email ?? ''))` logic also inlined in `AssigneeStep.tsx` (lines 103 and 107) and `ConfirmationStep.tsx`. The removed `getUserNameByEmail` helper previously provided this as a single source of truth.

Replace the inline expression with a call to a shared helper (e.g. `getUserNameFromDetail(assigneeFirstName, data?.assigneeEmail ?? '')`) so the fallback logic lives in one place.

Second occurrence of the duplicated `Str.removeSMSDomain(name ? name : (email ?? ''))` pattern in this same function. Both this line and line 103 repeat the logic that the deleted `getUserNameByEmail` helper used to own.

Consolidate into a single shared helper and reuse it here rather than duplicating the ternary + `removeSMSDomain` expression.

This inline `allMatchingQueryParams` computation duplicates the same all-matching-query logic added in `SearchTransactionsChangeReport.tsx` (`getAllMatchingQueryParams`). Both gate on `areAllMatchingItemsSelected && isEmptyObject(excludedTransactions) && currentSearchQueryJSON` and then build `{jsonQuery: serializeQueryJSONForBackend(currentSearchQueryJSON), hash: currentSearchQueryJSON.hash}`. Keeping two copies risks the branches drifting apart (this version also silently omits the `Log.warn` fallback the other has).

Extract a single shared helper (e.g. `getAllMatchingQueryParams(areAllMatchingItemsSelected, excludedTransactions, currentSearchQueryJSON)`) and call it from both files:

```ts
const allMatchingQueryParams = getAllMatchingQueryParams(areAllMatchingItemsSelected, excludedTransactions, currentSearchQueryJSON);
```

This new line re-implements logic that already exists in the shared `getCompanyCardFeed` helper (`src/libs/CardUtils.ts`), which does exactly `feedWithDomainID.split(CONST.COMPANY_CARD.FEED_KEY_SEPARATOR)` and returns the first element. The previous version of this function already delegated to `getCompanyCardFeed(feed)`. Duplicating the split-and-take-first logic inline means the two places can drift apart (e.g. if the separator handling or fallback behavior changes).

Widen the existing helper to accept a `string` (or add a thin string-typed variant) and reuse it instead of inlining the split:

```ts
// In CardUtils, accept string so callers with a bare string feed can reuse it
const feedWithoutDomainID = getCompanyCardFeed(feed);
```

This keeps the feed-parsing logic in one place.

This adds a second, separate call to `useLocalize()` (`const {formatPhoneNumber} = useLocalize();`) right next to the existing `const {dateFnsLocale} = useLocalize();` a couple of lines below. Calling the same hook twice duplicates work and is easy to consolidate.

Merge the two into a single destructuring call:

```ts
const {formatPhoneNumber, dateFnsLocale} = useLocalize();
```

The new `OpenPolicyRoomsPageOptions` type duplicates the exact five optional fields (`pageNumber`, `pageSize`, `sortBy`, `sortOrder`, `searchValue`) that were just added to `OpenPolicyRoomsPageParams`. Keeping two independent copies means every future change to the pagination/sort parameters must be made in both places or they silently drift apart.

Derive the options type from the params type instead of restating the fields:

```ts
type OpenPolicyRoomsPageOptions = Omit<OpenPolicyRoomsPageParams, 'policyID'>;
```

`ALLOWED_TRANSACTION_IMPORT_EXTENSIONS` hardcodes `['xls', 'xlsx', 'csv', 'txt', 'ofx', 'qfx']`, which duplicates the contents of the sibling `ALLOWED_SPREADSHEET_EXTENSIONS` (`['xls', 'xlsx', 'csv', 'txt']`) and the newly added `OFX_STATEMENT_EXTENSIONS` (`['ofx', 'qfx']`). If either source list is ever updated (e.g. a new spreadsheet extension is added), this combined list will silently diverge and the transaction importer will accept a stale set of extensions.

Derive the combined list from the existing sources instead of re-typing the values, e.g. compute it once as `[...ALLOWED_SPREADSHEET_EXTENSIONS, ...OFX_STATEMENT_EXTENSIONS]` so the three lists stay in sync automatically.

This app-load skeleton-gating logic duplicates `src/pages/inbox/sidebar/BaseSidebarScreen.tsx`. Both files independently derive `isLoadingHasLoadedApp = isLoadingOnyxValue(hasLoadedAppMetadata)`, compute the identical `isColdRestartRecoveryFallback = !hasLoadedApp && isLoadingApp`, and assemble the same `(!hasLoadedApp && (isAppLoadPending || isLoadingHasLoadedApp ...)) || isColdRestartRecoveryFallback` gate with the same explanatory comment (this file only additionally OR's in `isLoadingReportData`). Because the semantics are subtle (cold start vs. reconnect vs. account switch), maintaining two copies risks the two screens diverging when the gate is later corrected.

Extract the shared gate into a hook next to `useIsAppLoadPending` (e.g. `useShouldShowAppLoadSkeleton({includeReportData: true})` in `@hooks/useInFlightRequests`) and derive `isInitialLoad` from it, so both screens share one source of truth for this loading semantics.

This inline cast `route.params as {q?: string; name?: string} | undefined` duplicates the identical cast added in `SearchSidebar.tsx` (`route.params as {q?: string; name?: string} | undefined`). Both re-declare the same ad-hoc shape for the Search root route params, and both bypass the already-typed `SearchFullscreenNavigatorParamList[SCREENS.SEARCH.ROOT]` param list (which already declares `name?: string`), losing type safety.

Use the existing typed route hook instead of casting to a hand-written literal, e.g.:

```tsx
const route = useRoute<PlatformStackRouteProp<SearchFullscreenNavigatorParamList, typeof SCREENS.SEARCH.ROOT>>();
const searchName = route.params?.name;
```

This keeps the param typing centralized and avoids duplicating the same inline shape across `SearchTypeMenuNarrow.tsx` and `SearchSidebar.tsx`.

The copyable-text press/mouse-down handling introduced here is duplicated near-verbatim across many row components — `TransactionGroupListItem`, `TransactionGroupListExpanded`, `GroupHeader`, `TransactionListItemNarrow`, `TransactionListItemWide`, `SelectionList/ListItem/BaseListItem`, `Table/TableRow`, and `MoneyRequestReportTransactionItem`. Each repeats the same three-part boilerplate: a `wasMouseDownOnCopyableTextRef` ref, an `onMouseDown` that sets the ref from `isCopyableTextTarget(...)` and early-returns to skip `preventDefault()`, and a press handler that calls `shouldSuppressCopyableTextPress(...)` then resets the ref.

Extract this repeated logic into a shared hook (e.g. `useCopyableTextRowPress()` returning `{onMouseDown, shouldSuppressPress}` or a wrapped press handler) in `TextWithTooltip/selection` and consume it from each row component, rather than copy-pasting the ref + handler pattern into every list item.

The copyable-text selector string `'[data-copyable-text=true]'` is duplicated here (`copyableTextSelector`) and in `src/components/TextWithTooltip/selection.ts` (`COPYABLE_TEXT_SELECTOR`), and the `{copyableText: true}` dataset literal is re-declared as `COPYABLE_TEXT_DATA_SET` in at least five components (`MenuItem`, `TextWithTooltip/index`, `DisplayNamesTooltipItem`, `DisplayNamesWithTooltip`, `DisplayNamesWithoutTooltip`). These are all the same DOM contract copied around; a change to the attribute name would have to be made in every copy.

Consolidate: define the attribute name once in `CONST` (see CONSISTENCY-2) and derive the selector and dataset from it in a single shared location, then import that instead of re-declaring the literal in each file.

This is the fourth verbatim copy of the `getMoneyRequestParticipantOptions(...)` + `useParticipantsPolicyTags(participants)` block (also added in `useDistanceNavigation.ts`, `useOdometerNavigation.ts`, and `IOURequestStepDistanceGPS/index.native.tsx`), all with identical arguments. Duplicating this across four files is a DRY violation.

Extract the participant derivation and policy-tag lookup into a single reusable hook (e.g. `useMoneyRequestParticipantsPolicyTags`) that returns `{participants, participantsPolicyTags}`, and replace each of the four blocks with a call to it.

The same `getMoneyRequestParticipantOptions(...)` + `useParticipantsPolicyTags(participants)` block is repeated verbatim here and in `useDistanceNavigation.ts`, `useOdometerNavigation.ts`, and `IOURequestStepDistanceManual.tsx`. This duplicated logic should be consolidated so the argument list and lookup live in one place.

Move it into a shared hook (e.g. `useMoneyRequestParticipantsPolicyTags`) returning `{participants, participantsPolicyTags}` and consume that hook here.

This participant-derivation block (`getMoneyRequestParticipantOptions(...)` + `useParticipantsPolicyTags(participants)`) is identical to the one added in `useDistanceNavigation.ts`, `IOURequestStepDistanceGPS/index.native.tsx`, and `IOURequestStepDistanceManual.tsx`. Duplicating the same 9-argument call plus hook invocation across four files violates DRY and forces lockstep maintenance.

Extract a single shared hook (e.g. `useMoneyRequestParticipantsPolicyTags`) that computes `participants` internally and returns `{participants, participantsPolicyTags}`, and call it here instead of repeating the block.

This inline policy-ID resolution reimplements the same explicit-ID fallback chain that already exists as the canonical `getTransactionPolicyID` resolver in `src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts` (`[transaction.policyID, transaction.report?.policyID, transaction.policy?.id].find(...)` plus the unreported-report fallback). The PR description itself calls out that this should match `getTransactionPolicyID` "already used elsewhere," yet it is duplicated here. Duplicating this logic risks the two copies drifting apart (e.g. the ordering of fallbacks or the unreported-expense handling).

Reuse the shared resolver instead of hand-rolling the chain:

```tsx
import {getTransactionPolicyID} from '@libs/SearchUIUtils';

const effectivePolicyID = getTransactionPolicyID(transactionItem, policyForMovingExpensesID);
```

This keeps the unreported-expense fallback (`policyForMovingExpensesID`) behavior in one place and removes the parallel implementation.

This `filteredUnprocessedData.sort(...).map(...)` block (sort the default account to the top, then add a `borderBottom` separator under it when there is more than one item) is duplicated almost verbatim in `src/pages/workspace/companyCards/utils.tsx`. The only differences are the default-detection key (`creditCardAccountCode` vs `cardProgramAccount?.id`) and the value field. Consolidate the two copies into a single shared helper so the separator/ordering behavior only lives in one place.

Extract a helper (e.g. `sortDefaultAccountToTop(items, isDefault, styles)`) and reuse it in both this file and `utils.tsx` instead of repeating the sort/map inline.

This file is now a near-verbatim copy of `WorkspaceCompanyCardAddWorkEmailPage`. Both render the same `HeaderWithBackButton`, the same two `Text` nodes, and the same `FixedFooter` + success `Button` navigating to `ROUTES.SETTINGS_CONTACT_METHODS`; only the component/type name, `testID`, and `AccessOrNotFoundWrapper` feature props differ. This duplication means any future change has to be made in two places.

Extract a single shared `WorkspaceCardAddWorkEmailPage` component that accepts the differing values (`testID`, `featureName`, `policyFeature`) as props, and render it from both this page and the company-card page instead of maintaining two copies of the same JSX.

This new `getStringParam(params, key)` helper duplicates the sibling helper of the same name and purpose that already exists in `InboxTabButton.tsx` (same directory) — both safely extract a string param by key from an `unknown` params object. Keeping two copies (implemented slightly differently, one via `isRecord`, one via `Object.entries`) increases maintenance overhead and risk of divergence.

Extract a single shared helper (e.g. `getStringParam.ts` in this directory or a common navigation util) and import it in both `InboxTabButton.tsx` and `getReusableReportsTabStateKey.ts` instead of re-declaring it here.

The identical no-op fallback `const formatPhone = formatPhoneNumber ?? ((n: string) => n);` is duplicated across 6 files (`MoneyRequestBuilder.ts`, `PerDiem.ts`, `SendInvoice.ts`, `Split.ts` twice, and `Task.ts` twice). Every migrated function re-declares the same identity function to substitute for a missing `formatPhoneNumber`. This is copy-pasted logic that raises maintenance overhead — if the fallback behavior ever needs to change (e.g. to a shared default formatter), it must be edited in 7 places.

Extract the fallback into a single shared helper and reuse it everywhere the parameter is optional. For example, in `@libs/LocalePhoneNumber` (or a small local util):

```ts
// LocalePhoneNumber.ts
export const identityFormatPhoneNumber = (phoneNumber: string) => phoneNumber;
```

Then at each call site:

```ts
const formatPhone = formatPhoneNumber ?? identityFormatPhoneNumber;
```

This removes the duplication and gives the fallback a single, documented home.

The expression `isConciergeChatReport(chatReport, conciergeReportID) || isPolicyRelatedReport(chatReport, policyID)` is duplicated verbatim here and in `src/components/SettlementButton/index.tsx`, and the same workspace-membership check also appears in `src/pages/inbox/report/ReportActionCompose/SuggestionMention.tsx`. This logic previously lived in the now-removed `doesReportBelongToWorkspace` helper. Re-inlining it in multiple places violates DRY and means every future change must be applied in each copy.

Consolidate the check into a single reusable helper (e.g. a slimmed-down `doesReportBelongToWorkspace(report, policyID, conciergeReportID)` in `@libs/ReportUtils`) and call it here instead of duplicating the expression.

The whitespace-node filter (`tnode.children.filter((child) => !!child.tagName)`) plus the map through `TNodeRenderer` with the `` `${child.tagName ?? 'node'}-${index}` `` key and `renderIndex`/`renderLength` duplicates the same block in `TableRenderer.tsx` and `TableSectionRenderer.tsx`. Note `getElementChildren` at the top of this file also re-implements the same `!!child.tagName` filter.

Extract the shared filter-and-render logic into one reusable helper component and reuse the element-children filter (e.g. `getElementChildren`) everywhere rather than repeating `filter((child) => !!child.tagName)` in each renderer.

This filter-then-map-through-`TNodeRenderer` block (whitespace-node filter + `` `${child.tagName ?? 'node'}-${index}` `` key + `renderIndex`/`renderLength`) is identical to the ones in `TableRenderer.tsx` and `TableRowRenderer.tsx`. Consolidate this repeated logic into one shared helper so it lives in a single place.

Extract a shared `TableChildrenRenderer` component that filters element children and renders them via `TNodeRenderer`, then reuse it here instead of duplicating the loop.

This new file is a byte-for-byte copy of `src/pages/workspace/accounting/rillet/export/RilletCompanyCardAccountPage.tsx` (both resolve to the same git blob `8cdd725b270`). It duplicates the same component (`RilletCompanyCardAccountPage`), the same account list-building logic, and the same `updateRilletCreditCardAccount` call — none of it specific to selecting a per-card account.

Either implement the intended per-card-account selection logic here (reading/writing `NVP_RILLET_EXPORT_ACCOUNT` for the specific `cardID`), or if the two screens truly share behavior, reuse `RilletCompanyCardAccountPage` directly instead of duplicating the whole file.

The literal union `typeof CONST.POLICY.TYPE.TEAM | typeof CONST.POLICY.TYPE.CORPORATE | typeof CONST.POLICY.TYPE.SUBMIT` is duplicated verbatim across this PR in three files — `Policy.ts` (this line), `src/libs/actions/IOU/TrackExpense.ts:204`, and `src/libs/ReportUtils.ts:11594` — and it already appears elsewhere in `Policy.ts` (lines 266 and 2440). Repeating the same type expression in multiple places means any future change to the set of creatable workspace types has to be found and edited in every copy.

Extract it once into a shared named type and import it everywhere, e.g. in a common types module:

```ts
export type CreatableWorkspaceType = typeof CONST.POLICY.TYPE.TEAM | typeof CONST.POLICY.TYPE.CORPORATE | typeof CONST.POLICY.TYPE.SUBMIT;
```

Then use `type?: CreatableWorkspaceType;` / `policyType?: CreatableWorkspaceType;` in all call sites.

This per-report transaction-violations selector block (`transactionIDs` memo + `selectTransactionViolations` callback + the `useOnyx` subscription with `[transactionIDs]`), including the identical comment, is duplicated verbatim in `ApproveActionButton.tsx`, `PayActionButton.tsx`, and `SubmitActionButton.tsx`. Consolidate the shared logic into a single reusable hook.

Extract it into a shared hook (e.g. `useReportTransactionViolations(transactions)`) and reuse it here:

```ts
const [transactionViolations] = useReportTransactionViolations(transactions);
```

This per-report transaction-violations selector block (`transactionIDs` memo + `selectTransactionViolations` callback + the `useOnyx` subscription with `[transactionIDs]`), including the identical comment, is copy-pasted verbatim across `ApproveActionButton.tsx`, `PayActionButton.tsx`, and `SubmitActionButton.tsx`. Duplicated logic serving the same purpose should be consolidated (DRY).

Extract it into a shared hook (e.g. `useReportTransactionViolations(transactions)`) and call it from all three components:

```ts
const [transactionViolations] = useReportTransactionViolations(transactions);
```

This magic-code prompt implementation is duplicated almost verbatim in `Wallet/PersonalInfo/PersonalInfo.tsx`. Both files add the same `submittedPersonalDetailsRef`/`isConfirmingMagicCode` state, the identical `wasSubmittingRef` + `useEffect` submission-edge tracking, the same `isMagicCodeRequired` derivation, the same `confirmPersonalDetailsWithMagicCode`/`closeMagicCodePrompt` handlers, the same phone-change detection, and this exact `ValidateCodeActionContent` block with identical props.

Consolidate the shared behavior into a reusable hook and the shared prompt UI into a single component, then consume them from both KYC flows instead of copy-pasting the logic.

The expression `allPolicies?.[`${ONYXKEYS.COLLECTION.POLICY}${personalPolicyID}`]?.outputCurrency` is duplicated verbatim at two `changeTransactionsReport` call sites in this hook (here in `handleRegularReportSelection` and again in `removeFromReport`). Repeating this non-trivial lookup increases maintenance overhead if the personal-policy resolution ever changes.

Hoist it once near the top of the hook and reuse the local:

```ts
const personalPolicyOutputCurrency = allPolicies?.[`${ONYXKEYS.COLLECTION.POLICY}${personalPolicyID}`]?.outputCurrency;
```

Then pass `personalPolicyOutputCurrency` at both call sites.

This new tab duplicates logic already present in `src/pages/workspace/rules/AgentRulesSection.tsx`: the RuleBot resolution block (`ruleBotAccountID`, `ruleBot`, `ruleBotDisplayName`, `isRuleBotActiveMember`) and the `renderTitle`/`renderSubtitle` helpers are copied almost verbatim. This raises maintenance overhead and bug risk — a change to the "enforced by" line or the RuleBot naming fallback must now be made in two places.

The PR already extracted the sorting/visibility/title logic into `AgentRulesUtils.ts`; extract the remaining shared pieces too — e.g. a `useAgentRuleBot(policyID)` hook returning `{ruleBotAccountID, ruleBotDisplayName, isRuleBotActiveMember, ruleBot}` and shared `AgentRulesTitle`/`AgentRulesSubtitle` sub-components — and consume them in both `AgentRulesSection` and `RulesAgentsTab`.

This new `RoomMembersSearchBar` is a near-duplicate of the shared `Table.SearchBar` (`src/components/Table/TableSearchBar.tsx`). The `useLayoutEffect` focus logic, the unmount-cleanup `useEffect`, and the `SearchBar` render block are identical. The only addition is one `useEffect` that persists the phrase via `updateUserSearchPhrase(activeSearchString)`.

Don't fork the whole component for one extra side effect. Render the existing `<Table.SearchBar label={translate('selectionList.findMember')} />` in `RoomMembersTable` (as `ReportParticipantsTable` does), and handle persisting the search phrase in the page/hook that owns the search state instead of re-implementing the search bar.

This new `RoomMembersTableBody` component is a near-line-for-line copy of the shared `Table.Body` component (`src/components/Table/TableBody.tsx`). The imports, the `useBottomSafeSafeAreaPaddingStyle` setup, the `StyleSheet.flatten` min-height computation, `useDebouncedAccessibilityAnnouncement`, the `EmptyResultComponent`, and the entire `FlashList` render are identical. The only meaningful difference is the room-specific empty message returned by `getEmptyMessage`. Duplicating the whole component means every future fix to `Table.Body` has to be mirrored here.

Re-use the shared `Table.Body` instead of forking it. The room-specific empty message can be supplied via the existing `ListEmptyComponent` prop (already threaded through `listProps`), so `RoomMembersTable` can render `<Table.Body contentContainerStyle={styles.flexGrow1} />` like the other tables and delete this file. If a custom empty message is genuinely needed, prefer extending `Table.Body`'s empty-message handling rather than copying the component.

The two `<Button>` branches (the `!shouldShowAvatar` branch and the avatar branch below) duplicate almost the entire button configuration: `onPress={callFunctionIfActionIsAllowed(() => openExternalLink(calendarLink))}`, `sentryLabel={CONST.SENTRY_LABEL.ACCOUNT_MANAGER_BOOK_CALL.BUTTON}`, `accessibilityLabel={label}`, `isNested`, `medium`, and `style`.
